definition: Attention mechanisms that limit each token's attention computation to a subset of other tokens, rather than the full sequence, to reduce computational cost.
details: Sparse attention patterns (such as local windows or strided patterns) allow transformers to scale to much longer context lengths than standard full (quadratic-cost) self-attention would allow.
story: Think of an orchestra warming up: no single instrument carries the piece, but together they make the sound. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. The layout decides what the machine can even attempt, before it learns a single thing. The shape of the machine is half the idea. That blueprint is Sparse Attention.
